paragraphs: Children in care from Bromley live with carers approved by the council's own fostering team or by independent agencies such as those listed on this page. When the council launched its share of the national "Any of Us" recruitment film in October 2023, it said about 340 children were looked after in the borough.

To apply to Bromley you need to be over 21, have a spare bedroom and keep a smoke-free home. Short-term carers should live within about an hour of Bromley so children can stay in touch with family and friends. The council asks for two personal references, a medical report and enhanced DBS checks for adults in the household, runs a three-day preparation course, and aims to finish the assessment within 16 weeks before the case goes to its fostering panel.

Once approved, carers have a supervising social worker, a 24-hour out-of-hours phone line, membership of the Fostering Network, the Bromley Foster Care Association and small fostering hubs of six to eight families who meet to support each other. Carers who introduce a new fostering household receive £1,000 in vouchers once that household is approved.

Bromley publishes a weekly child allowance from £208 for children up to 4 to £309 for those aged 16 and over, plus a carer's fee of £206.66 a week for children up to 12 and £258.27 for those aged 13 and over. It also pays one-off sums at Christmas, for birthdays and for the summer holidays. The rates page does not say which year the figures cover, so check them with the fostering team.
If you live in or near Bromley, it is worth speaking to the council and to two or three of the agencies below, and comparing their training, support and pay before you decide.
